restore.future: This file comes from a newer HCN version. Update the app first.

notice.corrupt: data.json was damaged and no backup exists. The damaged file was kept as {{file}}

notify.title: HCN: {{over}} overdue, {{soon}} due soon
notify.hint: On launch and every 4 hours, HCN sends one summary of overdue and due-soon tasks not yet notified today.
notify.hint2: HCN notifies at each task's milestones. Each one fires once, and devices share what was already shown after syncing.
notify.testSent: Test sent. If nothing appears, allow notifications for HCN in the system settings.
notify.over: Alert when overdue and not done
notify.dayLate: Alert when past the end time and not done
notify.timeHint: Day-based reminders (before, on and after the deadline) arrive at the morning time. Anything during quiet hours waits until they end.
notify.bgHint: HCN must be running to remind on time. When on, clicking X hides the window to the system tray (by the clock); to quit, right-click the HCN icon > Quit.
notify.background: Keep running in the tray when closed
notify.androidHint: On the phone, reminders are scheduled by the system, so they arrive even when the app is closed or after a restart. If they're late, turn off battery saving for HCN.

people.hint: People are used to assign tasks and show avatars on the Gantt.
people.name: Name
people.empty: No one yet. Add the first person above.
people.deleteAssigned: {{name}} is assigned to {{n}} tasks. They will become "Unassigned".
people.duplicate: That name is already in the list

personal.hint: Used by the "My tasks" filter and as the default owner for new tasks.

data.backupHint: Save a .json backup, restore from a .json file (including backups from the old HTML version), or export a 4-sheet Excel file.
data.locationHint: Data lives outside the install folder, so updating or reinstalling keeps it. Automatic backups are in the backups folder.
data.legacyTitle: Move data from the old HTML version
data.legacyHint: Open the old HTML version, click Backup to get a cvkt-backup-….json file, then use Restore from .json above.
data.androidLocation: Data is stored in the app's private storage on this phone. Uninstalling the app deletes it, so sync with your PC or back up to .json first.

update.devNote: Development build: update checks only work in the installed app.
update.androidNote: On Android, update by installing the new .apk over the old one. Your data is kept.
update.androidHint: The app checks GitHub for a new version when opened (at most every 6 hours). Tap Download update, then tap the finished download to install over the current app; your data is kept.

wifi.unavailable: Sync is only available in the PC and Android apps.
wifi.hubHint: This PC acts as the hub: phones on the same Wi-Fi send and receive changes while the PC app is open. Data never leaves your local network.
wifi.enable: Allow phones to sync (Wi-Fi, USB, Bluetooth)
wifi.addressesHint: The phone only needs the pairing code — the app finds the address. Use these addresses to enter manually if needed; the label shows the connection type.
wifi.noAddress: This PC isn't connected to Wi-Fi or a wired network.
wifi.codeHint: Each code works once. It changes automatically after a phone pairs.
wifi.noDevices: No phones yet. On the phone: Settings > Sync, enter the code above and tap Connect.
wifi.removeMsg: {{name}} won't be able to sync until it pairs again. Data on the phone stays.
wifi.clientHint: On the PC: open HCN > Settings > Sync and turn sync on. On the phone, just enter the 6-digit code shown on the PC and tap Connect — the app finds the PC on the same Wi-Fi or over a USB / Bluetooth link.
wifi.auto: Syncs when the app opens, after changes and every 30 seconds while the phone can reach the PC running HCN. If the PC's address changes, or you switch between Wi-Fi, USB cable and Bluetooth, the app finds it again — no need to pair again.
wifi.unpairMsg: The phone stops syncing with the PC. Data on both devices is kept.

err.code: The pairing code is wrong or already used. Check the new code on the PC.
err.unpaired: The PC removed this phone. Pair again.
err.tooMany: Too many wrong attempts. Try again in a minute.
err.network: Cannot reach the PC. Tap Check connection to see why.
err.timeout: The PC does not respond (usually Windows Firewall). Tap Check connection to see how to fix it.
err.schema: The devices use different data versions. Update the app on both.
err.server: The PC reported an error. Try again later.
err.notFound: No PC found. Make sure HCN is open on the PC with sync on and both devices are on the same network, then tap Check connection.
err.firewall: Could not open the firewall (No may have been chosen in the administrator prompt). Try again, or ask someone with administrator rights.

wifi.tetherTitle: No Wi-Fi? Use a USB cable or Bluetooth
wifi.tetherHint: The phone shares a network with the PC over the cable or Bluetooth, then syncing works just like Wi-Fi. No Internet needed.
wifi.tetherUsb: USB cable: plug the phone into the PC, then on the phone turn on USB tethering (Settings > Connections & sharing, or Hotspot & tethering). Charging only or "File transfer" mode will not sync.
wifi.tetherBt: Bluetooth: pair the phone with the PC, then turn on Bluetooth tethering on the phone. On the PC: Bluetooth icon in the tray > Join a Personal Area Network > right-click the phone > Connect using > Access point. Bluetooth pairing alone does not create a network to sync over.
wifi.tetherThen: The new address then appears above (labelled USB cable / Bluetooth). A paired phone finds the new route by itself — nothing to re-enter.
wifi.found: Found {{name}} ({{addr}}). Enter the pairing code and tap Connect.
wifi.clientTether: No shared Wi-Fi: plug the cable into the PC and turn on USB tethering, or turn on Bluetooth tethering in the phone settings. Charging only, or Bluetooth pairing only, is not enough.
wifi.addrOptional: PC address (leave empty to find it)
wifi.foundN: Found {{n}} PC(s). Pick one (or leave empty to choose automatically), enter the code and tap Connect.
wifi.fixFwHint: Windows will ask for administrator permission — choose Yes.
wifi.publicWarn: Public networks (usually USB / Bluetooth links from the phone) are blocked by Windows Firewall until you open the firewall for HCN.
wifi.iphone: iPhone / iPad (Lightning cable): there is no HCN app for iPhone yet — the app is Android only (.apk), so an iPhone cannot install it or sync.

st.fw_ok: Windows Firewall lets phones connect, including over USB cable, Bluetooth and public Wi-Fi
st.fw_missing: Windows Firewall may block the phone over USB cable, Bluetooth or public Wi-Fi
st.fw_blocked: Windows Firewall is blocking HCN (usually because Cancel was chosen in the firewall prompt earlier)
st.fw_unknown: Could not check the firewall. If an antivirus with its own firewall is installed, allow HCN Work Manage there.
st.tray: Closing the window keeps HCN running in the system tray, so the phone can still sync (to quit: right-click the HCN icon > Quit)
st.loginOn: Starts with Windows: the hub is always ready after the PC boots
st.loginOff: Does not start with Windows: after a restart, HCN must be opened before the phone can sync

diag.title: Connection check
diag.netsUnknown: Could not read the phone's networks.
diag.netsNone: The phone only has mobile data (4G/5G): no Wi-Fi, USB or Bluetooth link to the PC.
diag.noProbes: Not paired yet, so there is no PC address to try.

ok.d: The PC answers normally. If new data is missing, tap Sync now.

addrChanged.t: The PC changed its address — found it at the new one
addrChanged.d: The app switched to the new address and synced again. No need to pair again.

noLocalNet.t: The phone is not connected to the PC
noLocalNet.d: Join the same Wi-Fi as the PC, or plug in the cable and turn on USB tethering, or turn on Bluetooth tethering (on the PC choose Join a Personal Area Network).

diffNet.t: The phone and the PC are on different networks
diffNet.d: The PC address is not on the phone's current network. Put both on the same Wi-Fi (not a guest Wi-Fi), or connect with a USB cable / Bluetooth as described.

firewall.t: Same network but the PC does not respond — usually the firewall
firewall.d: On the PC: Settings > Sync > "Open the firewall for HCN", then choose Yes. Company or guest Wi-Fi may stop devices talking to each other: try a USB cable.

hubOff.t: The PC is not accepting connections
hubOff.d: Open HCN on the PC and turn on "Allow phones to sync". If the PC just slept or restarted, open HCN again (turn on Start with Windows so you don't forget).

otherHub.t: The old address now belongs to another PC
otherHub.d: The app will not sync with that PC by mistake. Make sure your PC has HCN open and is on the same network as the phone.

notFound.t: No PC found on the network
notFound.d: Check that HCN is open on the PC with sync on; both devices are on the same Wi-Fi or USB / Bluetooth tethering is on; the firewall is open for HCN on the PC.

lists.catsHint: Used by monthly, weekly and daily tasks. Child tasks take their parent's category and can be changed afterwards. Shared with every synced device.
lists.placesHint: Used by daily tasks. A hidden item disappears from pickers, but existing tasks keep it.

lists.duplicate: An item with this name already exists
lists.deleteUsed: “{{name}}” is used by {{n}} tasks. Deleting clears it from them. To keep it on old tasks, use Hide instead.

pp.noAcc: Needs finished daily tasks with both planned and actual times.

v.late: {{n}} days past the deadline and not done
v.behind: {{p}}% behind plan · finish {{n}} more {{unit}} to catch up
v.nodates: Set start and deadline dates to compare with the plan

cancel.title: Cancel {{n}} task(s)?
cancel.msgNgay: The task and the time already worked are kept; it just no longer counts as work to do. You can restore it at any time.
cancel.msgParent: Unfinished child tasks are cancelled too; finished ones and worked time are kept, and progress at cancellation is preserved. You can restore at any time.
cancel.reasonPh: e.g. Client put the project on hold
cancel.locked: This task is cancelled: restore it before changing status or timing.
cancel.bannerHint: Progress, finished child tasks and worked hours are kept for reference.
